_comment: Dataset barriers. ARCHITECTURE.md is the prose; this file is the part a
machine checks. layer_audit.py reads it and enforces two rules: one
writing process per file, and no module writing across a layer boundary
Layer membership follows what a file is a record OF, except that anything
derived, regenerable and never hand-edited is Layer E regardless of which
layer it summarizes. That one convention is what makes the crossing rule
enforceable: without it every audit and every model would legitimately
touch three layers and the rule would mean nothing.

A.name: Facilities
A.subject: Existing and operating data centers.
A.key: facility_id (planned); today the snapshots have no stable key

B.name: Proposed projects
B.subject: Announced, proposed and under-construction projects, and their lifecycles.
B.key: project_id (prj_<source id>); the permanent key is pk in data/project_key_map.csv (project_key_map.py, 2026-09-29)

C.name: Opposition events
C.subject: Recorded opposition events and the entities that produce them. Joins to Layer B only through the existing entity linkage.
C.key: opp_id, linked to project_id through data/project_links.csv

D.name: Policy instruments
D.subject: Enacted and pending restrictions, the county frame they attach to, and the reference geography that frame is built on.

E.name: Derived analytics
E.subject: Everything computed from the layers above: baselines, models, audits, worklists, reports. Declared derived, never hand-edited, always regenerable from its inputs.
E.key: inherits the key of whatever it was derived from

exempt_multi_writer.master_opposition.csv: The source of record for Layer C, and the one file with more than one writer by design. scripts/build_master_csv.py refreshes it from upstream under the ownership rule that ended the 2026 corruption; census_gap_candidates.py and promote_signal_candidates.py append gated promotions only. All three are append-or-refresh under a stated ownership discipline, none of them rewrites another's rows, and every promotion lands in an audit trail. This exemption is the reason the rule exists elsewhere: it is the exception that had to be argued for.
exempt_multi_writer.data/signal_candidates.csv: A handoff, not shared ownership. signal_harvest.py writes the queue; promote_signal_candidates.py consumes it and rewrites what remains, so the file holds exactly the rows the gate did not promote. The two never write concurrently: the promoter runs after the harvester in the same workflow.
exempt_multi_writer.data/restriction_verification_worklist.c: A handoff, not shared ownership. restriction_verification_worklist.py builds the rows and preserves every reviewer column across rebuilds (merge on fips); legistar_probe.py only fills the reviewer columns of open rows it finds an adopted restriction for, and rewrites the file only on a hit. They run in sequence in one pipeline step, the probe first, so the builder always re-exports the probe's hits. Declared 2026-09-29.
exempt_multi_writer.data/project_links_manual.csv: apply_link_suggestions.py appends auto-applied links; project_id_rekey.py (one-time, by a person) and project_key_map.py (after every scrape) rewrite only project_id cells whose project the source renumbered. None of them adds or removes another's rows.

declared_crossings.signal_harvest.py: Layers A and C. One GDELT call returns both facility-lifecycle articles and opposition coverage, and splitting the network call in two would double the quota cost to separate what a single classifier can route. The module routes, it never merges: a row lands in exactly one layer's file, with the opposition side winning any tie, and neither file is a source of record.
declared_crossings.census_gap_candidates.py: Layers C and D. This is the gap-closure promotion path: a Layer D census gap becomes a Layer C opposition record. The crossing is the point of the module and it is gated (complete, dated, sourced, dedup-guarded, census-corroborated), appends only, and writes every promote, hold and block decision to data/gap_promotion_report.csv.
declared_crossings.status_resolution.py: Layers C and E. The scan proposes only: it writes data/status_resolution_worklist.csv (Layer E) and changes nothing in Layer C. --apply writes master_opposition.csv (Layer C), but only from data/status_resolutions.csv, the reviewer-confirmed file that names the evidence URL and confirmation date for each change; a headline never changes a status by itself. It is idempotent, matches rows on normalized Source URL, and deletes nothing (superseded rows stay in master and are held out of the clean feed by hold_superseded). Declared 2026-09-28 with the module.
declared_crossings.project_id_rekey.py: Layers B and E. Run by a person with --apply (CI runs it report-only), it rewrites the source-id key of hand-maintained Layer B files (overlay, decision dates, manual links, duplicates, negative-audit codings) after the source renumbers, and writes its own Layer E report. It changes only the id column, only on rows whose git-blame time and text agree on the project, and writes every decision to data/pipeline_intel_rekey_report.csv. The crossing is the repair: without it the hand files follow the number instead of the project.
declared_crossings.project_key_map.py: Layers B and E. After every scrape it rewrites only the id cells of the hand-maintained Layer B files (overlay, decision dates, manual links, duplicates, negative-audit codings) whose project the source renumbered, matched on identity through the permanent key in data/project_key_map.csv, and writes its own Layer E report. Ambiguous matches, orphans and unknown ids are held for a person, a scrape missing more than 15% of known projects writes nothing, and a hand re-pointed row is never reverted (Ruling 5, 2026-09-28). It is the standing replacement for project_id_rekey.py's one-time repair.
declared_crossings.clean_opposition_data.py: Layers C and E. The cleaner writes the Layer C change log (change_log.csv, one row per edit it makes to a record) and its own Layer E diagnostics (data_quality_report.md, counts and checks over the cleaned feed) in the same pass, because the report describes exactly the edits that run made. It never writes another layer's source of record. The write was always there; the audit first saw it on 2026-09-29, when it learned to follow default output parameters.
declared_crossings.fetch_pudl.py: Layers D and E. The county generation features (data/county_pudl_features.csv and its manifest) are Layer D reference data beside data/county_census_features.csv; the data/_pudl_*.parquet files are its Layer E download cache, kept so a rerun does not refetch PUDL. The cache only feeds the feature build and is never read as a record. First seen by the audit 2026-09-29 (default output parameter).

_comment: Files a module writes but CANNOT rebuild from scratch, because they are
append-only or carry hand-seeded rows a regeneration would not reproduce.
layer_audit.py --write-gitattributes excludes these. The distinction is
load-bearing: a fully derived artifact should conflict and be regenerated,
because a clean three-way merge of two independent regenerations splices
them into a file neither run produced. An append-only file is the opposite
case, where a three-way merge is exactly right: two branches each appending
different rows is a merge git performs correctly and a conflict would be a
not_regenerable.data/external_restriction_census.csv: Append-only. refresh_external_census.py --promote appends gate-passing rows and never rewrites the file, and the census also carries hand-seeded rows (IU ERI publishes counts without a machine-readable list) plus hand corrections that no regeneration reproduces.
not_regenerable.master_opposition.csv: The Layer C source of record. Written by three modules under the ownership rule that ended the 2026 corruption, all append-or-refresh, and hand-edited besides.
not_regenerable.data/signal_candidates.csv: A handoff queue, not a derived artifact: signal_harvest.py writes it and promote_signal_candidates.py rewrites what remains after promotion.
not_regenerable.data/restriction_evidence_history.csv: Append-only grade-change log. Its value is that earlier rows are never rewritten, so a regeneration would destroy the history it exists to hold.
not_regenerable.data/census_promotion_report.csv: Append-only audit trail of every promote and hold decision, for the same reason.
not_regenerable.data/feature_search_weight_history.csv: Append-only. One row per variable per weight update, carrying the observation, its standard error and the filtered state; the filter's state file (feature_search_weights.json) can be rebuilt from it, it cannot be rebuilt from the state file.
not_regenerable.data/feature_search_weights.json: Filter state carried between runs. Each run updates the previous state rather than recomputing from scratch, so a regeneration from the current data alone would reset every weight's history to a single observation.
not_regenerable.data/project_key_map.csv: Minted keys and their first_seen dates cannot be rebuilt: a regeneration would renumber every key.
not_regenerable.data/project_key_aliases.csv: Every id, slug and name each key has carried, accumulated run by run.
not_regenerable.data/layer_b_anchors.csv: Which key each hand-file row was written about. Rebuilding it from today's ids would re-anchor any row a renumbering had already moved.
not_regenerable.data/facility_graduation_observations.cs: First-observation dates; the earliest date is kept and a scrape-dated observation cannot be recovered once history is gone.
not_regenerable.data/proposal_candidates_news_log.csv: Append-only run log. proposal_discovery.py appends one row per run (queries, articles, failures) and never rewrites it, so two branches' runs merge correctly line by line. Registered 2026-09-29 when the write map first saw it.
Append-only run log. fetch_air_permits.py appends one row per run and never rewrites it. Registered 2026-09-29 when the write map first saw it.
not_regenerable.data/facility_candidates_osm_log.csv: Append-only run log. fetch_osm_facilities.py appends one row per Overpass run (states queried and failed) and never rewrites it. Registered 2026-09-29 when the write map first saw it.
not_regenerable.data/restriction_probe_log.csv: Append-only probe log. restriction_probe.py appends each probe attempt and never rewrites the file; it is the audit trail of what was asked of which portal. Registered 2026-09-29 when the write map first saw it.
